payload.title: Crete Wedding Packages and What They Include
payload.audience: Couples in their 30s interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, AUD 150k+ budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, often with parents contributing, planning a Crete wedding for guests flying in from Australia. They have narrowed down a few Crete resorts and estates, east around Elounda or west around Chania, and are now holding package documents that share a name but not a shape: one bundles a ceremony set-up and coordinator, another sells use of a space for set hours, a third expects a planner to bring the rest. They want to know what a Crete venue package really covers, what sits outside it, and how to put two quotes side by side before they pay a deposit.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation so an advisor can compare the couple's shortlisted Crete venue packages like for like, with the quote in AUD and inclusions confirmed in writing.
payload.angle: Crete wedding packages look alike in a search result and differ on paper. Page-one results lead with prices and adjectives; this guide shows, only from what each Crete venue publishes about its own package, what sits inside (ceremony set-up, coordinator, spaces and hours), what is charged on top or left to the couple (guest rooms, exclusive use, extra hours, outside suppliers, documents), and where a venue fee, a venue package and a planner each begin and end. It turns those gaps into a like-for-like quote checklist an Australian couple can take into any proposal. No figures, so the comparison stays true when prices change.
must_include: Direct answer in the first 100 words: a Crete venue package usually bundles the ceremony set-up, a coordinator and set hours in a space, while guest rooms, exclusive use, extra hours and outside suppliers vary by venue; link /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-venues and /destination-weddings/wedding-in-crete prominently in the intro.
Exactly 4 Key takeaways, each one sentence, no figures.

Types of Crete package: ceremony-only, ceremony and reception bundles, named tiers, exclusive-use or space hire, elopement or packages for two, each tied to a Crete venue that publishes it (venue names allowed only where their package is described), in fresh wording.
What packages include: each inclusion attributed to the venue that states it, written plainly without research talk; venue paperwork offers only as that venue's own offer, mentioned once each.

What is left out or charged on top, written as questions to ask, using 'charged on top' or 'a fee applies' only where a venue says so: exclusive use, guest rooms and minimum nights, extra hours, outside suppliers and supplier rules, documents.

Ceremony type inside a package: religious, civil and symbolic as venues state them; 'symbolic ceremonies are not legally recognised in Greece' only as Elounda SA's brochure states it; link /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions once; nothing implies the Wedded Advisor handles legal, church or religious paperwork.
Venue package vs venue fee vs a planner: practical trade-offs, no planner or vendor names.
East vs west Crete only where the source pack's facts support it; otherwise omit the section.

Comparing two quotes like for like: checklist covering inclusions in writing, deposits and cancellation, exclusive use and days, music times, weather plan, level access, quote currency and contract language, no figures; the single body Advisor line follows it.
Legal in brief (as at November 2026, from the Euphoria legal facts in part-5), linking /destination-weddings/wedding-in-crete for the steps rather than repeating them.
Australian angle: is the quote in euros or AUD (as a question); deposit and cancellation terms as questions; travel insurance only as a question.

One Advisor line in the body plus the close, from brand-facts.md only: one Wedded Advisor as a single point of contact, quotes in AUD for Australian couples, inclusions confirmed in writing before the couple commits.

Links: /destination-weddings/crete-wedding-venues (prominent), /destination-weddings/wedding-in-crete (prominent), /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages, /destination-weddings/greece-wedding-packages-all-inclusive, /destinations/europe/greece, /expert-advice/greek-wedding-traditions (once), /wonderland-concierge and /magazine with UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=crete-wedding-packages&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing (Concierge and magazine only). Anchor text says 'Wedded Concierge', never 'Wonderland Concierge'.
avoid: Any price, fee, euro or AUD amount, 'from' price, percentage, per-person figure or deposit size anywhere, including FAQ, meta and alt text.

Research talk ('on its own site', 'in its own words', 'does not publish' as our search, page dates as source talk, myths sections); 'often told' more than once; hedge stacking; linking any source more than once.
'Best' claims, best month, ranking packages; calling a package all inclusive unless the venue says so.
Stating a legal meaning not in an official source or the venue's own brochure; any Advisor role in legal, church or religious paperwork.
Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; Wedded Privileges; 'free'; transfer offers in copy; the brand-facts.md Advisor tagline line (never reuse its closing phrase).
Planner or other vendor names; venue contact or business details; implied partnerships or preferred rates.
Reading or citing Elounda Beach (declined earlier); competitor sites, directories, planner blogs, review sites or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording, claims or images.
Em dashes, US spelling, exclamation marks, clichés, keyword-stuffed headings.
AI images of any venue, destination or wedding; unlicensed images (placeholders only).
Repeating the Crete venues guide's venue profiles, the Wedding in Crete guide's legal steps or the all-inclusive comparison's venue-by-venue table; summarise and link instead.

payload.intro_plan: Open on the reader's real problem (two Crete package documents that look alike but are not), give the direct answer in the first 100 words, then link the Crete venues guide and the Wedding in Crete guide.
key_takeaways_plan: A Crete venue package usually covers the ceremony set-up, a coordinator and set hours in a space, and the rest depends on the venue.
Guest rooms, exclusive use, extra hours and outside suppliers are where Crete packages differ most, so ask about each in writing.
A venue fee, a venue package and a planner each cover different ground, so check who is responsible for every part of the day.
Compare quotes on the same guest count, spaces, hours, nights and currency before paying any deposit.
